title: proto: Allow formatted string from packet details in columns
description:
Add a column setting to use the formatted string from packet details
in custom columns instead of the value or resolved names.

This is useful in some situations where the formatted string gives
better information.

Changed the existing "Resolve Names" setting to select between
- Display as Values
- Display as Strings
- Display as packet Details

Future enhancement - now that packet details can be displayed, add a dfilter function for it. Complement to `vals`.  
https://www.wireshark.org/docs/wsug_html/#_functions  
`vals:   Converts a field value to its value string, if it has one.`

Currently for `FT_BYTES` fields, the code reports that they can't be resolved, which keeps the GUI from allowing that flag to be toggled. In fact slightly different output is produced in the two cases, with and without a byte separator.

The different behavior can be forced by editing the preference file manually and changing the character indicating the resolution status.

The current code defaults to setting `col_resolved` to true, whereas this change makes it so that the names (the equivalent of the old `U`) is the default. That means that bytes fields now default to having a byte separator instead of no separator. (Neither before or after this change is it possible to toggle through the GUI.)

Not sure what the correct behavior is.
I added a separate commit with a workaround to keep "resolve names" for custom columns which does not have "resolve names". This reverts back to the original behaviour.

If `FT_BYTES` is the only case, it might work to just have `column_prefs_custom_display_names` (the former `column_prefs_custom_resolve`) in `preference_utils.c` just claim that `FT_BYTES` can be "resolved" (an increasingly inaccurate term) and I think it might then switch between the with and without byte separators version.

I had a question on Discord if we should always enable "Resolve Names", even if they don't show a different value. This will give us less complex code and may give benefits we haven't seen.

I think renaming could help on the inaccurate term issue, but I haven't found the right words yet. I'm still open for suggestions.

- Display as Value
- Display as String representation
- Display as packet Details
@johnthacker Did you have a look at the FT_BYTES exception and the renaming?

The column header context menu is not allowing `Display Values`.  
Editing the column and setting `Display: Values` works.
The workaround had some issues. I have reverted this and added `FT_BYTES` as a special case, and renamed "Display Names" to "Display as Strings".

Looks better now.  
Could the [tooltip](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/17269/diffs?file=32852ec97387d1b1803aa074d00c19f0282acc3b#32852ec97387d1b1803aa074d00c19f0282acc3b_118_118) in [column_editor_frame.ui](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/3026adefa8d196d02b48ebb59535ef0ed95519f0/ui/qt/column_editor_frame.ui) be added as a tooltip on packet_list_header.cpp context menu selections?  


> Values will show the raw values for fields.
> 
> Strings will show human-readable strings instead of raw values for fields. Only applicable to custom columns with fields that have value strings.
> 
> Details will show the value using the same format as in Packet Details.
Added tooltip.

Thanks! Last comment: :-)  
The default alignment for Strings and Packet Details is Left.  
For Values, default it Right.  
For long fields like `tls.handshake.type` I lose the `1` when switching between display types.  
I've thought that there should be a preference for what the default alignment is for new custom columns but haven't seen anyone else mention it so never opened an enhancement.  
  
Thanks for the updates to this MR after I "kicked the tires".  
  
(`tls.handshake.comp_methods_length` is one that flips the `1` left/right).
I think the default column alignment should be handled in a separate MR. You can always manually set the column alignment to match your flavour.
